title: A shared language for people and AI agents: the semantic layer, component by component
description:
A shared language for people and AI agents: the semantic layer, component by component

In March 2026, Gartner announced that semantic layers are a non-negotiable foundation for Enterprise AI, and that by 2030 they will be treated as critical infrastructure for all data shops.

The timing follows a change in who consumes enterprise information. As AI models and agents take on that role, what an organisation records has to be readable by machines and humans alike, across every silo.

The semantic layer is not a single platform. It is a stack of components that give an organisation a shared, machine-usable understanding of its own knowledge:

Knowledge assets: structured data, unstructured content and processes, all connectable
Business glossaries: one meaning for a concept across divisions
Metadata: the context around every asset
Taxonomies: hierarchies that people and systems can both navigate
Ontologies: the how and why behind relationships between concepts
Knowledge graphs: those relationships applied to real data, forming a traversable web

This session explains how the pieces work together, then shows the layer in action through cases from a global financial services firm, an investment management agency, a global services organisation, and a product and retail organisation.

It draws on the book Bridging Knowledge, Data, and AI, published in May and described as the first dedicated exclusively to the semantic layer and how it is implemented.

Pitched at beginner to intermediate level, for business professionals with some technical understanding. Attendees leave knowing what the semantic layer is, what it contains, and how to lead the initiative in their own organisation.
